competencies.title: Actors and actor isolation
competencies.summary: Can explain how actors protect mutable state, reason about reentrancy, and use them correctly instead of as locks.
coverageTopics: reentrancy and interleaving at suspension points
when an actor is the wrong tool
mistakes: treating an actor as a mutex that blocks other callers
assuming state cannot change across an await inside an actor method
wrapping every type in an actor rather than isolating the shared state

competencies.title: MainActor and UI isolation
competencies.summary: Can explain what @MainActor guarantees, where isolation is inherited, and how to move work off and back onto the main actor correctly.
coverageTopics: why DispatchQueue.main.async is usually the wrong reach in modern code
await hopping back to the main actor
Task { } inheriting actor context vs Task.detached
mistakes: believing @MainActor makes code run synchronously on the main thread from anywhere
using Task.detached and then wondering why UI updates warn
annotating an entire service with @MainActor to silence warnings

competencies.title: async/await fundamentals
competencies.summary: Can explain suspension, how await differs from blocking, and how async functions compose.
coverageTopics: suspension points and what await actually does
async functions do not block a thread
calling async code from synchronous contexts
mistakes: describing await as blocking the thread
assuming two sequential awaits run concurrently
thinking async implies a background thread

competencies.title: Recognising and fixing data races
competencies.summary: Can spot unsynchronised shared mutable state and choose an appropriate fix.
coverageTopics: what makes an access a data race
why 'it works on my device' is not evidence of safety
mistakes: assuming a crash-free run proves thread safety
adding a lock around reads but not writes
